focus: CC-WP-02 standalone-vs-production canonicalizer acceptance blind spot

coordination.prior_obligation: Parse current admitted G9+Dialect through both identity paths using one production parser constructor and separate semantic identity from parser/grammar contract identity.
coordination.nonduplication_delta: This follow-up advances that obligation with an implementation candidate, direct gate coupling and an actually executed Lark placeholder lesion/rescue mechanism test.

finding.interpretation: The terminal WP02 closure could pass a standalone canonicalizer component and a production frontend canonicalizer receipt independently even though they used different Lark optional-placeholder construction semantics. Commit comparison shows tools/claycode_base_canonicalizer.py was not modified between the terminal PASS and the current diagnosis, so this is not a post-PASS revert.
finding.scope_guard: This proves an evidence-coupling defect and parser-construction divergence. It does not by itself prove downstream persisted-hash corruption or justify WP02 promotion.

changes: Standalone canonicalizer reuses claycode_base_frontend.build_parser and rejects synthetic None children.
Standalone receipt records maybe_placeholders=false and explicit absent-optional guards.
New cross-canonicalizer probe executes the standalone CLI and compares full G9/Dialect canonical syntax hashes to the same canonicalizer fed by the production parser constructor.
Production BASE canonicalizer validation now consumes the cross-parity result so the existing WP02 closure cannot pass the two paths independently.
Ubuntu pull-request workflow executes strict cross parity, production validation and selected-WP02 strict closure preflight.
candidate.rollback: Close PR 153; main production files remain unchanged until independently executed candidate evidence exists.

hypothesis: Direct cross-path parser-construction parity is necessary because independently green canonicalizer receipts can hide a semantic-tree construction mismatch.
counterhypothesis: Independent standalone canonicalizer PASS plus production canonicalizer PASS are sufficient; direct parity coupling adds no unique defect detection.

exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.name: IN_MEMORY_OPTIONAL_PLACEHOLDER_CONTRACT_LESION_RESCUE
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.purpose: Deliberately restore Lark optional-placeholder behavior in memory, then rescue with the production absence contract to test whether the proposed tripwire has a lesionable falsifier.
exactly_one_out_of_box_experiment.minimal_grammar_features: record declaration with [] optional type-parameter and [] optional field default
limitations: This local experiment uses a minimal reproducer, not the full V17/G9/Dialect checkout.
Exact PR 153 execution remains required before merge or promotion.

external_evidence.official_lark: Strict mode can report ambiguity/collisions, but advanced regex lookaround can escape interegular collision analysis; explicit metamorphic and parser-contract tests remain required.

architecture_delta.decision: Keep PR 153 draft until exact candidate bytes execute on an admitted Linux/Ubuntu lane. Do not relabel parser/grammar contract identity as cognitive semantic identity. Trace persisted hash consumers before any rename/migration.

targeted_distribution.claycode: Consume PR 153 as the executable realization of the already distributed WP02 identity-layer parity obligation; preserve V17/V19 selection as a separate lane.
targeted_distribution.unifieddb: Continue tracing persisted syntax/semantic/contract hash consumers before migration; this run does not establish downstream corruption.
targeted_distribution.harness: No change; parser contract drift remains provenance/version evidence, not Frank cognitive semantic change by itself.

next_falsifier: Execute PR 153 exact bytes on a step-executing Ubuntu/Hostinger lane; require strict full G9+Dialect cross-parity PASS, mutation detection/rescue PASS, and full selected-WP02 closure PASS. If PASS, compare persisted hash consumers before deciding merge/migration; if FAIL, preserve the first exact counterexample.
